First off this oil has a bit more gardenia than rose to it, but it's just the top notes and wears off after a little bit. Then you can smell the subtle scent of roses mixed with the memory of the gardenia as it still lingers within the scent. review: LumaRx facial cleaning brush is like a Sonicare ElectricToothbrush for the face. After moistening my face and the brush heads with water, I tested the sensitive and normal heads with both soap and [[ASIN:B01648QDS4 L'Oreal Paris Age Perfect Facial Cream Cleanser, 5 Fluid Ounce]] and the massaging head with water alone. After a one-minute "application" with any one of the brushes, I love how smooth and clean this makes my face feel.  The packages includes:  - three brush heads (sensitive, normal, and massage) and their covers which have air vents to hasten drying - one charging base with power cord - one brush wand that operates at 3 speed levels - one white plastic zippered travel case - one instruction pamphlet  PROS:  - The wand contains a rechargeable battery that last for 30 uses. The first charge takes up to six hours.  It also has a 30 minute fast-charge feature that will provide 4-5 uses. By the way, I love the charging light on the base; it has a "cool" factor to it.  - There's a one minute timer that has what I call a "tripacer" (like Sonicare's quadpacer) timer built in for each of the three zones of the face. These zones are the T zone, left side, and right side. What this means is that the unit pauses ever so slightly ever twenty seconds to let the user know when it's time to move on to the next zone so that the cleaning time can be distributed evenly among zones.  - None of the three brushes were rough or extremely abrasive. The rotating and vibrating brush heads were as gentle as could be and I have sensitive skin.  - The wand with brush can be used in the shower as long as it's not fully submerged in water.  - This can be used to remove cosmetics.  - The unit comes with a 2-year limited warranty.  CONS:  - Although these brushes remove make-up effectively, I personally only like to use this on the days I do not wear makeup. The reason is that the eye area has to be avoided. I use eye makeup so I wind up washing my entire face with my hands instead as it does not make sense to me to use a brush on only part of my face.  - There are a lot of don'ts in the manual like don't submerge in water, don't use around the eyes, don't use if you are taking steroid-based medication, don't operate outdoors or where there are aerosol products or oxygen being administered, etc.  - If used daily at no more than the maximum two times per day, the brush heads need to be replaced  every three months. The Massaging head (since it doesn't not have bristles) can be replaced every six months. This can get expensive. I contacted the company for the replacement price and they said they would let me know when it's orderable on Amazon. I will update the comments section of this review with that information when I receive it.  - The battery on this unit is NOT replaceable as per the email from them which I posted in the comments section of this review.  At first I questioned why would I need such a facial cleansing tool. After using this, however, I realized that I love how it makes my face feel so clean and smooth. This is not a tool I would use more than twice per week since I really hate using this to remove makeup, however, it's so gentle on my skin that I look forward to the cleansing action, mildly exfoliating properties, and the light massage it provides me all without the use of a chemical masque

review: Vague Label Ingredients, But Lathers Well, Smells Good. I am pretty picky when it comes to my body washes. I like one that has good ingredients, and a great smell. When I saw the label for this saying Argan Oil, Coconut Oil and Tea Tree Oil, I knew it would be right up my alley. I love all 3 of those ingredients and they work well with my skin. I was excited to use this. When it arrived and I checked the ingredients label, I was shocked. Like so many other reviews, I don't see any of the above listed on the label. Some ingredients are very vague. Some of the ingredients I had never heard of before and had to look up. My suggestion to the company is to make the label a bit more descriptive and clearly put what is inside. What essences? What type of vegetable oils? Since it is so unclear, if you have easily irritated or sensitive skin I would stay away from this. The vague label makes it hard to use by anyone who may have allergies to certain things. After the blades are completely dry, I run the blades over my forearm *with the blades* to sharpen them with my own skin. review: Not a loofah, but still a great wash cloth.. This is a great wash cloth, but it's not a loofah, so the name might be a little misleading to some. review: These are exactly what I need them to be. These are great!  No seriously, I'm thrilled to have these.  If you're like me and you make your own lotions and creams and scrubs and such, then you absolutely NEED these, at a good price, in pretty much exactly this size and here's why.  If you make lotion and you've done the tiniest bit of research, then you know the preservatives debate/dilemma/controversy and that's this--if you're going to have a big bottle or jar of lotion out on the counter, then it NEEDS a preservative.  But all the preservatives have twelve-syllable unpronounceable names, and people who like to keep their stuff a little bit more on the natural side don't like to use them.  And if you're like me and you don't mind the long names of whatever chemical you have do use to preserve it, you're never 100% positive you got the right amount.  Too much, and the lotion is unusable and irritating.  Too little and you can get bacteria, mold and yeast growing in your lotion, and that's lousy.  So if you don't want to use a preservative, everybody advises you to keep your lotion in the fridge.  Which is great, but what, I want to get out of the shower, trek out to the kitchen, use my lotion, and then put it back while I'm in a towel?  Enter these cool little things, which hold a couple of days worth of cream, which is exactly how long I feel okay having an unpreserved lotion out of the fridge.  So I make my lotion, pour 24 ounces of it into these little things, and pull one out every couple of days.  Really good deal.  Hope they're dishwasher safe.  I received these at a discount in exchange for an honest review, and I chose to review them because I expected them to be good, and they are

review: It’s a decent idea, it worked, but not with the included suction cups. I drive my wife nuts when I trim my beard in the bathroom - I try to catch all the clippings, but without something like this, it does not work well. I thought I”d give this a try - it seems like a great idea, but...  1. It arrived with 1 plastic bib, 2 suction cups with hooks, and 1 shaving cream brush. 2. The plastic bib feels okay - it’s a thin plastic, but it should last for a decent amount of time. It is not as nice as most of the kinds I’ve experienced or we own for haircutting 3. Its stitching is okay - I think it’ll last decently 4. There are two loops on the ends you will attach to the suction cups. 5. The suction cups - are worthless. This is why it gets the 4 stars - I would have given it 3 stars if we didn’t have our own suction cups to use instead of theirs. One of the two that came with it stuck for 5 - 10 seconds before it stopped working altogether. The other suction cup doesn’t even look right - it looks like it never worked and was not made properly. 6. We have suction cups (bought on Amazon) we were able to use - I looped that part of the bib onto them, which worked, but not designed for this, they would fall off. I’ll end up taping them to it - at least that way I’ll be able to use it. 7. It fit me fine. It felt fine - just like a haircut cape. The white looks weird - I’m used to the far more common black - but at the same time I think it’ll show the beard hair really well. 8. I did notice that as I go in closer to the mirror to see what I’m doing it folds over in front of me and isn’t as trapped out - be aware of this because it’s easy to start missing the catch in the bib.  Overall it’s a decent thing to have and it’ll make my wife happy not getting the beard clippings all over the place. This could be a little nicer -  a little thicker plastic, much better suction cups - which would easily earn it a 5 star rating. But for what it is, I’m happy to have it. If it lasts, it’ll be great

review: I like this but.... My only complaint with Zest isn't unique to that product:  it has to do with the downsizing of consumer products so companies don't have to raise their prices; they just give us less.  Zest comes in a 4 oz bar, common in most "bath sized" bars but smaller than I remember bars of soap when I was a younger man.  The smaller the bar, the easier it is to drop it when it's wet.  If you get beyond that, Zest has two strong positives:  the scent is pleasant without being overpowering.  It is appropriate for men but I don't think women would object to using it as well.  Also, it appears to be less caustic when you wash your face around your eyes.  I made the mistake of getting Coast Soap in my eyes once and almost had to see a doctor; this is much milder.  The bottom line:  I will continue to buy Zest and will keep whining about small bath bars.  This is a decent soap brand.  Update:  I originally wrote this about the 4 oz bars and the review somehow got applied to the larger 5 oz bars as well.  Please allow me to make this clear:  the 5 oz bars answers all the negatives I had about the smaller bars.  This is finally what I've been looking for and I couldn't be happier with the larger size. review: creamy semi matte finish, bold, bright pop of color, fades w/ drink & food, smudges. Not shiny, not matte, somewhere in between. They call it semi-matte, and I agree. But anyone who has lines or parched lips, should always avoid any formulation with the word "matte" in it. You are better off with a lip liner and a moisturizing lip gloss or lip stick. Matte will always dry down and make the lip skin pucker a little. My lips aren't wrinkled, but I can tell the formula pulls the skin together a little.   The color is bold. 06 Crush Berry appears to be a blue based red. Definitely red, like a classic red, just blue based rather than orange based. It feels super smooth on the lips, not at all tacky. Doesn't feel or look dry to start, but it dries down to a matte look. Can achieve a decent level of stain with a few applications and blotting.  The first pass has a more oily look and feel to it. I smash my lips one way, and it appears to come off lips a little. Then I smash them in the other direction, and the color is there again. But once it sets, it isnt budging like that again. Any color disappearance is from drinking, eating.  The case looks and feels good. The overall product is pretty good, just comes down to wanting a bold semi matte color that will perform like most other lipsticks- wears off with drinking & eating.Even then it doesnt disappear. Just might need to even out the color after awhile.  It seems to hold up to the product description. So for that (and all else), I give it a solid 4 stars.  I'm not in love with it, but it looks nice in pictures. Has a bright pop of color. This is not a subdued look at all. I find that it nearly matches a bold lip tint that I like by "I'm Meme"  https://www.amazon.com/dp/B091GSRN78/

review: A little pricy, but worth it -- the color and design are beautiful, and the barrette is great for thick hair. I don't know why Made in France barrette fixings are so superior to anything made in the United States -- they certainly look the same and mechanically, they function the same, but for some reason, the French barrettes are just a whole lot better.  They don't pull or catch my hair, they don't stretch out of shape, they don't break and bend.  I know this is a lot of $$ to spend on a barrette when you can get one for a fraction of this price at your corner drug store, but these France Luxe barrettes are worth it.  This coral colored scallop design is beautiful, and the barrette hold a lot of hair.  This is definitely for thick hair.  France Luxe also makes boule style barrettes for fine hair -- so if you don't have a thick mop, I would check out the other France Luxe designs. review: Can this be my new signature scent?. Wow. Okay. Wow. This product is absolutely phenomenal. It is absolutely worth the scary 30 dollar price tag. I cannot believe how good this stuff is. review: Did not work for me. Let me begin this review by stating that I have been using Egyptian, Indian and Pakistani 100% henna for over 30 years with beautiful results that lasted a full 3 months.  I decided to try this product because I wanted a change from all the red highlights and thought it would be nice to tone down to a browner hue.  I not only followed the instructions to the letter, but had several exchanges with the seller to make sure what I was doing was correct.  The good news is that this combination beautifully toned down the red from all my prior years of using henna only.  The bad news is that NOT ONE gray hair (I'm dark brown with about 15% gray) gave up being gray! So in addition to the hassle, mess and expense of doing this treatment (and make no mistake - it's messy and time consuming) I will have to double up this month and do my regular henna only routine.  I did a bit of research, by the way, and learned that most henna/indigo distributors, unlike Harvest Moon, suggest mixing up the henna and indigo powders SEPARATELY and then combining.  Based on my experience, I'd have to say this would probably work better (the rationale probably being the same as why combining shampoo and conditioner together don't work as well as shampooing and THEN conditioning).  Likewise, everyone else except Harvest Moon recommends wrapping the hair in plastic wrap and then covering with a shower cap and leaving on for a MINIMUM of 2 hours (Harvest Moon says their product works in less than one hour and is against wrapping.) review: So far this is working well for my sensitive skin; will see how it goes in the long run. First off, I have extremely sensitive skin overall, but especially on my face. To that end, I must be very carefully about what I put on. I do tend towards lighter or no scents, but have found some that work alright for me. But with or without scent, I can still have issues. In the end, it’s how my skin handles anything that is the bottom line for me. In this case, this Provence Beauty Beard Oil - All Natural Fragrance Free Olive, Sunflower & Jojoba Oils works well for me and so far, I’m very pleased.  I use a derma roller a couple times a week to help with hair in my beard and front of my head. At this point I then add a beard oil to these locations to help stimulate growth. Without doing major testing with all the elements, like a control group (area) of my head, it’s hard to say what works and what doesn’t. I feel like the derma roller has a large part in how well growth or at least slowing of loss goes. But, I have also come to believe some of these oils available do play a supportive role. To that point, I won’t be able to speak about this Provence Beauty Beard Oil - All Natural Fragrance Free Olive, Sunflower & Jojoba Oils  for awhile. review: excellent ingredients, could use more packaging info, works well w/ shamp & conditioner. I like the shampoo and conditioner a lot- leaves my hair soft, manageable, and healthy looking. I added in this serum as I hoped to gain hair density or at least reduce loss (or reduce cycle frequency and/or duration). I dont have trouble growing my hair, I have trouble keeping it. So my hair is long, but much less dense than previous years. I transitioned from minoxidil to this. I wont do that again, as any gains I got from minoxidil were lost-- and I do contribute some of that to not using this as consistently as I did that. I'll explain what went into that below. This serum helped the condition of my hair and scalp, so I think it works well with minoxidil instead of in lieu of it. I likely wont continue with the serum for a few reasons.  1. there was no instruction as to how to use this product. It is a dropper bottle, and I pretty much just used it like I did with minoxidil-- massaged whatever I pulled with dropper and distributed all over scalp, primarily at crown. Was this the correct way to do it? no idea. *  2. It does say to apply to clean hair. Well, many of us do not wash our hair every single day. I have long curly hair that leans dry and there is no need to wash it daily. So I am either applying this to unwashed scalp daily or it only gets applied a few times a week.  Hence the lack of consistency. So right here it eliminates some would-be users if it has to be on a fresh washed scalp.  3. the dropper is uncomfortable. I do not want to drop it from the dropper. I want to run it across the scalp so as to keep it from getting on my hair. The dropper is a little sharp feeling (at least my bottle that I received). I like the dropper style, and my thought is that if I were to buy this again, I would use a dropper from an old minoxidil bottle instead.  4. How long should this bottle last? Since I had no idea how much I should use, I often wondered if I used too much or too little. Any new hair treatment needs to be given 4-6 months of consistent use to see results, if any. I know the shampoo and conditioner helped, and this serum has great ingredients that will help existing hair and scalp health.. but the inconsistency on my part from lack of instructions as well as expectation of using on fresh washed hair made it impossible to see if I could get benefit from it.   * "It is best applied to damp hair after showering. We recommend visually splitting your scalp into 4 sections/quadrants. Depending on the amount of hair, use around 3-5 drops per quadrant. I like to drop into fingers and work into scalp. The remaining amount on your fingers you can work through your hair. It is perfectly fine to use the serum many times a day. That being said, it is important that the scalp/hair is clean" (--I saw this written in the community question section of this page. Including this on box or in a leaflet would have been greatly helpful)  The ingredients are of quality, the products work well together. I have since gone back to minoxidil, and once I have stopped the current shedding phase, I may buy another bottle to use as a support product. For that, I give it 4 stars

review: Good.  However, probably not for oily skin. This foundation has potential IF you use a good primer with it.  I have combination skin and, like many foundations, this can settle into pores and creases.  Some foundations are better than others in terms of this tendency, and I'd say this one is about "par for the course" with regard to settling in pores and creases.  Primer will help.  This does seem to have a lot of moisture in it (as I've found with many foundations that have "satin" in the title).  For me, I feel a bit dewy and not quite clean enough in this -- especially when I look in my 10X magnification mirror.  However, I'd venture to guess that people with dry skin might actually appreciate this.  Whereas people with oil prone skin and/or visible pores -- will NOT appreciate this so much.  I ordered the Fair color and I'm an NC20 or NC25.  The color is great (not orange and not pink).  Nice neutral color.  It was just slightly lighter than my natural skin color and looked great with a light dusting of bronzer / blush.  I always prefer to err lighter than my natural color than to go to darker, and end up looking like and orange pumpkin.  NOTE  >>>Be sure to shake this well before each use<<<  I noticed if I don't shake this, the first spray is mostly moisture and has a shiny greasy effect.  Product applies much better if it is well shaken first.  This should be in bold print on the front of the can.  I spray this into a little eyelash tray (or back of hand, or where ever) and dab my make-up brush into it.  Then, apply to face.  Its a good foundation.  However, getting up into this price point, I felt some of the above minor gripes warranted removing a star

review: Love the Coconut Baby & will try others.... ***  Just received the Limited Edition "Sugar Cookie" in the mail today.  My 21-month-old daughter is already asking for a bath while yelling "yummy" -- yes, it smells great! *****  I first tried Sweet Baby Organics Shampoo & Wash in Coconut Baby for my daughter last fall when she was 10 months old.  I liked the scent right away, but I was also impressed with the fact that it rinsed so clean.  I have tried other natural and organic baby washes with a coconut base, and they seemed to leave a "film" on my baby -- I liked that this formula was rich, and thick, without being sticky.  It's true that the foaming is minimal when comparing Sweet Baby Organics to washes with chemical lathering agents (such as SLS) but I found the lather from the coconut base to be "just right" without being bubbly.  We live in Kenya, so when I buy on Amazon I have to wait for my family to send me a box in the mail, or for someone to come over to visit (last fall I brought a supply of it back in my luggage).  My next package arrives in April, and this time we are trying the Vanilla Baby scent. The shampoo is NOT tear-free, but again, that is because of the lack of numbing chemicals in it's formulation -- I simply hold one hand over my daughter's forehead, and rinse her hair with a cup of clean water in my other hand.  One other fact to note is that a little goes a long way.  At first I was concerned that there were only 8oz bottles available, but even at 15 months old, a dime-sized amount cleans my daughter's entire head and body (though I have to admit that being a blondie, she doesn't have a whole lot of hair yet)

review: BBs are revolutionary, this makes it easy to find out why. I had heard that BBs were the new rage but my brain was stuck on the need to match my skintone to the makeup, so I didn't feel comfortable buying it online if I couldn't see the color. Buying this kit helped me to realize that my hesitation over color was a silly concern. While it does look like foundation, it does not behave like foundation. I'm not sure what it uses to create the effect but I'm going to say that rather than pigment, it contains some sort of magical light diffuser. Up close, you cannot tell you are wearing any makeup. You can still see your sunspots and tone issues. However, step away from the mirror and suddenly they all disappear and your skin looks dewy and spot free.  This is as revolutionary to makeup as Spanx was to the fashion world.  You're wearing makeup but no one can tell. Brilliant!!!  Although the color is not something you need to worry about, the package does allow you to experiment with the different types of BBs that are out there.  Some offer more coverage than others, some don't work as well with oily t-zones.  I will definitely be purchasing a full size BB from this kit and am glad I took the risk to try the products. Additionally, the shipping from the seller was very fast. I ordered another sample kit from the Mischa (sp?) brand and it's been 2 weeks and I still haven't received it. review: Wet, slippery fun...i mean massage. I have seen "massage oils" before, but this one is definitely legitimate. The jug that came in will last for a LONG time, especially considering it doesn't take much at all. The trick is, which is stated plainly on the bottle, to have damp skin when you use this. Coming out of the bottle, it's a viscous, gel. The picture i took doesn't show it well because my camera is slow, but pressing just a little bit between my fingers left a long string between them (much longer than the picture). Once you add water, it is more liquid. I would suggest keeping a spray bottle nearby if you're going to use it for a longer period of time since once your skin isn't damp, it gets tacky pretty quickly (hence the four star). We figured out keeping warm water nearby so the person receiving the massage doesn't get blasted with cold water at random. That is not relaxing, at all. Other than that, there was little to no smell, i did not try tasting it because...eww. I'm a chicken and won't even taste test the flavored massage gels though, so that can't be held against this one. Main tips: Keep warm water nearby (preferably in spray bottle) and GET PLASTIC SHEETS. I didn't even think about it when i ordered this, but had to run out to...wait for it...Lowe's so i can test this gel out.
